topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

row.title: Comparative economic analysis of crop yield under organic and conventional farming systems in Punjab, Pakistan
row.authors: Waqas Aslam, Rana Shahzad Noor, Saif Ullah, Hong Chen
row.treatment_description: Organic farming (natural manure, minimal pesticides)
row.control_description: Conventional farming (NPK fertilizers, synthetic pesticides)
row.notes: Survey of 300 farmers (153 organic, 147 conventional) in 2019. Parenthetical values in Table 4 interpreted as SE based on large sample sizes (SE with n~90 gives realistic CV~15%). row.title: Effect of organic farming on the restoration of soil quality, ecosystem services, and productivity in rice–wheat agro-ecosystems
row.authors: Panwar AS, Ansari MA, Ravisankar N, Babu S, Prusty AK, Ghasal PC, Choudhary J, Shamim M, Singh R, Raghavendra KJ, Dutta D, Meena AL, Chauhan GV, Ansari MH, Singh R, Aulakh CS, Singh DK, Sharma PB
row.treatment_description: Organic crop management (FYM 7.84 t/ha, vermicompost 3.13 t/ha, neem cake 853 kg, Sesbania green manuring)
row.control_description: Inorganic crop management (DAP, muriate of potash, urea; recommended NPK doses)
row.notes: Organic rice yield significantly HIGHER than inorganic. Data averaged across 4 locations and 15 years (2004-05 to 2017-18). LSD is for crop management main effect comparison. n not explicitly stated; design has 3 reps at each of 4 locations = 12 plots per treatment per year, averaged over 15 years. Organic management included Sesbania green manuring which likely boosted rice yield.

row.treatment_description: Organic crop management (rice + wheat combined, organic inputs only)
row.control_description: Inorganic crop management (rice + wheat combined, synthetic inputs)
row.notes: System productivity (REY) difference between organic and inorganic is NOT significant (difference 143.7 kg/ha < LSD 496.0). row.authors: David, C., Celette, F., Abecassis, J., Carcea, M., Friedel, J.K., Corre-Hellou, G., Hiltbrunner, J., Messmer, M., Narducci, V., Peigné, J., Samson, MF., Schweinzer, A., Thomsen, I.K., Thommen, A.
row.outcome: Grain yield (wheat) - organic range vs conventional range
row.treatment_description: Organic farming (no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides)
row.control_description: Conventional farming (synthetic inputs allowed)
row.notes: NO EXTRACTABLE QUANTITATIVE DATA. This is a review/survey paper, NOT an original experimental study. Table 2 reports organic yield RANGES by country (France: 2.5-5.0, Denmark: 1.0-4.0, Austria: 3.0-5.5, Italy: 3.5-6.0, Switzerland: 3.0-6.5 t/ha) but no single-point means. The text states conventional yields range 6-8.2 t/ha (Eurostat) and organic yields are '30% to 70% of conventional', but these are aggregated literature/statistical summaries, not paired experimental observations. No variance, sample sizes, or individual study-level data are reported. Table 1 describes crop rotation systems only. This paper should be EXCLUDED from the meta-analysis as it provides no primary quantitative observations suitable for effect size calculation.

topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

row.control_description: No conventional farming control present. This paper is an intercropping study WITHIN organic farming only.
row.notes: CRITICAL: This paper does NOT match the organic vs conventional PICO. ALL treatments are under certified organic management. Variance: only Tukey letter notation (a, b) at P≤0.05; no numeric SE/SD reported. Error bars visible in Fig 1 but values not stated. n=4 replications per treatment per year, 2 years averaged. This paper should be EXCLUDED from an organic vs conventional yield gap meta-analysis.

row.notes: 2014 year. All 8 subpopulations from same RCBD trial with 4 reps. No per-group SE/SD reported in paper; only mixed-model REML estimates available (Table 5: residual SD=0.12 t/ha). topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

row.control_description: AFS-CON: Conventional agroforestry, Cavendish banana planted 10/2010 at 4x4m
row.notes: Mean marketable yield ± SE from Table 1. HEAVILY CONFOUNDED: AFS-SUC has different banana varieties, lower planting density (8x8m vs 4x4m), and more competition from higher diversity of associated species. Text: banana yields in AFS-SUC much lower partly due to lower planting density and different varieties. Coffee yields also significantly lower in AFS-SUC. This yield gap is primarily due to system design, not organic vs conventional management.

moderators.mod_crop_species: banana (Musa x paradisiaca - mixed varieties in SUC, Cavendish in CON)

row.title: Meteorological fluctuations define long-term crop yield patterns in conventional and organic production systems
row.authors: John R. Teasdale & Michel A. Cavigelli
row.outcome: Corn grain yield (least squared mean, ANCOVA-adjusted for precipitation and heat stress)
row.treatment_description: Organic corn (3 rotations pooled: 2-yr corn-soybean, 3-yr corn-soybean-wheat, 6-yr corn-soybean-wheat-alfalfa-alfalfa-alfalfa; legume cover crops, alfalfa, poultry litter for N; USDA NOP standards)
row.control_description: Conventional corn (2 systems pooled: no-tillage and chisel-tillage; herbicide and fertilizer programs, genetically modified cultivars)
row.notes: Least squared means from ANCOVA adjusting for precipitation and heat stress covariates, not raw means. n values are total plot-year observations across all systems and years within each management group. Paper reports 31% yield reduction. When weed cover added as additional covariate, gap reduced from 31% to 16%. 1999 data excluded (extreme drought killed crops); 2003 conventional corn excluded (wet weather prevented standard management).

moderators.mod_soil_type: silt loam (Christiana, Matapeake, Keyport, Mattapex series)
moderators.mod_analysis: ANCOVA with precipitation and heat stress as covariates

row.authors: Herrera JM, Levy Häner L, Mascher F, Hiltbrunner J, Fossati D, Brabant C, Charles R, Pellet D
row.outcome: Grain yield (network-wide mean across all sites and years)
row.treatment_description: Organic management (OM): ~90 kg N ha-1 as liquid manure, no synthetic pesticides or mineral fertilizers, 380 seeds m-2, 11 sites, 1998-2018, 102 genotypes total
row.control_description: Conventional low-inputs (LM): 150 kg N ha-1, no fungicide, 350 seeds m-2, ~10 sites, 1998-2018, 300 genotypes total
row.notes: CAUTION: Organic and conv-low networks were at different sites with different genotypes. The 33.5% gap overstates the true system effect. With common genotypes in last 3 overlapping years, HM-OM=20.23 and HM-LM=14.32 dt/ha, so LM-OM=5.91 dt/ha (~8.4% gap). Overall means: OM=46.86 from 11 organic sites, LM=70.40 from ~10 LM sites. 3 replications per plot at each site. Units: 1 dt/ha = 100 kg/ha.

moderators.mod_note: Networks conducted at DIFFERENT sites with DIFFERENT genotypes and partially overlapping time periods; yield difference of 23.54 dt/ha includes site and genotype confounding. With common genotypes in last 3 years, OM-LM gap narrows to ~5.91 dt/ha (p<0.05), suggesting most of the 33% gap is confounded.

topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion

tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion

extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately

4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration

tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)

5. Record crop species and study duration

Significance letters: NB='a', Control='b'.

row.treatment_description: BGA + FYM (organic, two amendments combined)
row.control_description: Recommended chemical fertilizer N80P40K40
row.notes: Mean of 3 years (2003-2006). CD(5%) = 0.48 t/ha is pooled LSD.

topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year combination separately
2. Treatment = ORGANIC system; Control = CONVENTIONAL system
3. If multiple crops compared, extract EACH crop as separate observation
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) for meta-analysis weighting
5. Record crop species and study duration
6. Convert all yields to consistent units (prefer kg/ha or Mg/ha)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

row.authors: Y. V. Singh, B. V. Singh, S. Pabbi and P. K. Singh
row.treatment_description: Azolla + BGA + FYM + Vermicompost (organic, all four amendments combined)
row.control_description: Recommended chemical fertilizer N80P40K40
row.notes: Mean of 3 years (2003-2006). CD(5%) = 0.48 t/ha is pooled LSD. All four organic amendments combined - yield at par with chemical fertilizer (difference 0.33 t/ha < CD 0.48). This is the most complete organic system and the most relevant comparison for organic vs conventional meta-analysis.
